problem: Public routes could inherit different historical shell dimensions, allowing header, navigation, footer and mega-menu geometry to drift by route.
root_cause: Multiple generations of site chrome retained different width and height values while the live V18 shell had become the effective production authority.
decision: Make V18 production chrome the single geometry authority and enforce route-to-route browser parity.
prevention: Never add route-local geometry overrides for header, navigation, footer or mega-menu.
All new public routes inherit the canonical shell.
Representative routes are compared in browser regression checks.
A geometry contract change requires same-lineage skill, docs, learning and System Map updates.
